conditions.tensor_storage: owning allocation from the declared native allocator

binary_evidence.fact: Requests <=511 bytes become 512. The ordinary branch computes (size+511)&~511. The power-of-two-division branch is entered only when size>divisions*512 and rounds to a subdivision interval that is therefore at least 512 bytes. Every normalized block size is a multiple of 512.
The normalized size from local -0x2a0 is stored at offset +0x30 of the AllocParams object beginning at -0xf0; the same object is passed to alloc_found_block.

The function saves AllocParams+0x30 as the split size. It assigns that size to the allocated Block and advances the remainder Block pointer field at +0x48 by exactly that size while subtracting the same amount from remainder size. Repeated splits therefore add only multiples of 512 to the original base pointer.

A new native segment is obtained through the installed MACA device allocation path. The installed public two-argument device-allocation contract states that returned linear memory is suitably aligned for any kind of variable.

proof: Base device allocations are at least 4-byte aligned by the installed runtime contract. Every native caching-allocator split offset is a sum of normalized sizes, each divisible by 512 and therefore by 4. By induction, every native Block base returned for a fresh owning storage remains at least 4-byte aligned, including blocks reused after splits.
scope: Explicit source scenario carried through RuntimeInputs and the same virtual storage. No inference from simulator process environment or a single observed pointer.
excluded: A tensor view or alias with nonzero storage_offset is not covered; contiguous layout alone does not imply storage_offset==0. A BF16 view offset by one element can shift an aligned storage base by 2 bytes and fail the 4-byte predicate.
Other allocator backends, expandable-segment configurations, externally supplied storage, IPC/imported pointers, and historical Serving-process allocator/config state are not covered.
The one observed runner data_ptr is corroboration only and is not used as the guarantee.
The initially unset cached-flag condition is a declared target-process input, not proof of a historical Serving process.
Argmax reduction flags, typed instructions, dynamic branch counts and rates are separate contracts.
No production duration, actual historical provider or normal-memory acceptance is derived.
